extracted.intended_audience: researchers, faculty, students, and others interested in NIH peer review and grant-review research
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizing and evaluating the earliest-stage NIH peer review practice in which reviewers provide preliminary criterion scores and an overall impact score that determine which applications advance to discussion; the page reports findings about racial disparities in those scores. Useful for readers interested in peer-review measurement and equity in funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary criterion scores
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers provide initial criterion scores for applications during the earliest stage of NIH peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These preliminary criterion scores are used at the initial review stage and, according to the study, racial disparities in these preliminary criterion scores fully explain racial disparities in preliminary overall impact scores. They thereby influence which applications progress to the discussion stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary overall impact scores
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers assign a preliminary overall impact score for each application at the initial stage of review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary overall impact scores are used along with criterion scores to determine which applications go on to the discussion stage. The paper finds that disparities observed in these overall impact scores are accounted for by differences in preliminary criterion scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer weighting of criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: How reviewers weigh the relative importance of different preliminary criterion scores when forming the preliminary overall impact score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study examined whether differences in reviewers' weighting of criterion scores explain black–white differences in preliminary overall impact scores and found that such differences in weighting do not appear to explain the observed disparities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of initial scores to select applications for discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure whereby initial criterion and overall scores determine which applications advance from the preliminary stage to the discussion stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The earliest-stage scores (criterion and overall impact) are operationally important because they are the gatekeepers for which applications receive further consideration; thus, bias at this stage has substantial downstream consequences for funding outcomes.
